tasks.title: Configure MySQL Database and Enhance NewsArticle Entity
tasks.description: Update the project configuration to connect to a MySQL database as required by the PRD, and update the NewsArticle data model to include all specified fields.
tasks.details: The current implementation uses an in-memory H2 database and an incomplete NewsArticle model. This task involves adding the MySQL dependency, updating application.properties with the correct datasource configuration, and modifying the NewsArticle.java entity to include fields: `author`, `publicationDate`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. The `id` should be changed to UUID, and `@CreationTimestamp`/`@UpdateTimestamp` annotations should be used for automatic timestamping.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the application starts successfully and connects to the MySQL database. Inspect the database schema after startup to confirm the 'news_article' table is created with all the correct columns and data types.

subtasks.title: Update Maven Dependencies for MySQL
subtasks.description: Modify the `pom.xml` file to include the MySQL database driver and remove the H2 in-memory database dependency.
subtasks.details: In the `pom.xml` file, locate the `<dependencies>` section. Remove the dependency block for `com.h2database:h2`. Add a new dependency for the MySQL connector: `mysql:mysql-connector-java` or the newer `com.mysql:mysql-connector-j`.
subtasks.testStrategy: After updating the pom.xml, run `mvn clean install` or sync the project with your IDE to ensure the new dependency is downloaded and the old one is removed without build errors.

subtasks.title: Configure MySQL Datasource in application.properties
subtasks.description: Update the `application.properties` file to switch from the H2 configuration to the new MySQL database connection details.
subtasks.details: In `src/main/resources/application.properties`, remove or comment out the existing H2 properties (`spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb`, `spring.h2.console.enabled=true`, etc.). Add the following properties for MySQL, replacing placeholder values as needed: `spring.datasource.url=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/your_database_name`, `spring.datasource.username=your_username`, `spring.datasource.password=your_password`, `spring.datasource.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver`. Also, add `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update` to allow Hibernate to manage the schema.
subtasks.testStrategy: Start the application. Check the console logs for successful connection messages to the MySQL database. The application should start without datasource-related errors.

subtasks.title: Change NewsArticle Primary Key to UUID
subtasks.description: Modify the `NewsArticle` entity to use a UUID for its primary key instead of a Long.
subtasks.details: In the `src/main/java/com/example/api/model/NewsArticle.java` file, change the type of the `id` field from `Long` to `java.util.UUID`. Update the `@GeneratedValue` annotation from `strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY` to `strategy = GenerationType.UUID` to automatically generate UUIDs for new entities.
subtasks.testStrategy: After the changes, restart the application. Inspect the database schema to confirm the `id` column in the `news_article` table has a type compatible with UUIDs (e.g., `binary(16)` or `varchar(36)`).

subtasks.title: Add Author and Publication Date Fields to NewsArticle Entity
subtasks.description: Enhance the `NewsArticle` entity by adding the `author` and `publicationDate` fields as specified in the requirements.
subtasks.details: In `src/main/java/com/example/api/model/NewsArticle.java`, add two new private fields: `private String author;` and `private java.time.LocalDate publicationDate;`. Generate the corresponding getter and setter methods for these new fields.
subtasks.testStrategy: Restart the application and inspect the `news_article` table schema. Verify that new columns `author` (e.g., `varchar(255)`) and `publication_date` (e.g., `date`) have been created.

subtasks.title: Implement Automatic Timestamps in NewsArticle Entity
subtasks.description: Add `createdAt` and `updatedAt` fields to the `NewsArticle` entity and use Hibernate annotations for automatic timestamping.
subtasks.details: In `src/main/java/com/example/api/model/NewsArticle.java`, add two new private fields: `private java.time.Instant createdAt;` and `private java.time.Instant updatedAt;`. Annotate the `createdAt` field with `@CreationTimestamp` (from `org.hibernate.annotations`) and the `updatedAt` field with `@UpdateTimestamp`. These fields should be non-updatable from the client side, so you can make the columns non-updatable in the `@Column` annotation if desired (e.g., `@Column(updatable = false)` for `createdAt`).
subtasks.testStrategy: Restart the application. Inspect the `news_article` table schema to confirm the `created_at` and `updated_at` columns exist (e.g., as `datetime` or `timestamp`). Later, when the create/update endpoints are built, verify these fields are populated automatically.

tasks.title: Implement Create News Article Endpoint (POST /api/v1/news)
tasks.description: Create the API endpoint for adding a new news article to the system. This corresponds to the 'Create' part of the CRUD requirements.
tasks.details: Implement a method in `NewsArticleController` mapped to `POST /api/v1/news`. This method will accept a JSON representation of a new article in the request body. The corresponding service layer logic in `NewsArticleService` will handle the persistence of the new entity using `NewsArticleRepository`. The endpoint should return the newly created article with a `201 Created` status.
tasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test that sends a POST request with a valid article payload. Assert that the response status is 201 and the response body contains the created article's data, including a generated ID and timestamps. Test with an invalid payload to ensure a 400 Bad Request is returned.

tasks.title: Implement Retrieve Single Article Endpoint (GET /api/v1/news/{id})
tasks.description: Create the API endpoint to fetch a single news article by its unique identifier.
tasks.details: In `NewsArticleController`, add a method mapped to `GET /api/v1/news/{id}` that accepts a UUID as a path variable. The service layer will use the repository to find the article. If found, return the article object with a 200 OK status. If not found, it should result in a 404 Not Found status.
tasks.testStrategy: Create an article in the test database. Send a GET request using its ID and assert the response is 200 and the body matches the article. Send another GET request with a non-existent ID and assert the response is 404.

tasks.title: Implement Basic List Articles Endpoint (GET /api/v1/news)
tasks.description: Create the initial version of the endpoint to retrieve a list of all news articles. This will serve as the base for adding pagination and sorting.
tasks.details: Based on the existing skeleton `NewsArticleController`, fully implement the method mapped to `GET /api/v1/news`. This method will call the service to fetch all articles from the repository and return them as a JSON array with a 200 OK status.
tasks.testStrategy: Populate the test database with several articles. Send a GET request to the endpoint and assert that the response is 200 and the returned JSON array contains all the created articles.

tasks.title: Add Pagination and Sorting to List Endpoint
tasks.description: Enhance the `GET /api/v1/news` endpoint to support pagination and sorting as specified in the PRD.
tasks.details: Modify the list articles endpoint to accept `page`, `pageSize`, and `sortBy` query parameters. Use Spring Data's `Pageable` interface in the controller and repository. The `sortBy` parameter should handle field names and direction (e.g., 'publicationDate:desc'). The response should be a `Page` object or a custom DTO containing the list of articles for the current page and pagination metadata (totalPages, totalElements, etc.).
tasks.testStrategy: Test pagination by requesting different pages and sizes, asserting the correct subset of data is returned. Test sorting by requesting sorting on `title` and `publicationDate` in both `asc` and `desc` order and verifying the order of the results.

tasks.title: Implement Update Article Endpoint (PUT /api/v1/news/{id})
tasks.description: Create the API endpoint to modify an existing news article.
tasks.details: Implement a method in `NewsArticleController` mapped to `PUT /api/v1/news/{id}`. It will take the article ID from the path and the updated article data from the request body. The service logic should retrieve the existing article, update its fields, automatically update the `updatedAt` timestamp, and save it. Return the updated article.
tasks.testStrategy: Create an article, then send a PUT request with updated data. Verify the response is 200 and contains the updated data. Fetch the article again to confirm persistence. Test updating a non-existent article to ensure a 404 is returned.

tasks.title: Implement Delete Article Endpoint (DELETE /api/v1/news/{id})
tasks.description: Create the API endpoint to remove a news article from the system.
tasks.details: Implement a method in `NewsArticleController` mapped to `DELETE /api/v1/news/{id}`. The service should find the article by its ID and delete it. A successful deletion should return a `204 No Content` status. If the article to be deleted is not found, it should result in a 404 status.
tasks.testStrategy: Create an article, send a DELETE request with its ID, and assert the response status is 204. Attempt to GET the same ID and assert a 404 is returned. Test deleting a non-existent ID to ensure a 404 is returned.

tasks.title: Implement Global Exception Handling
tasks.description: Implement a centralized exception handler to ensure consistent and informative error responses across the API.
tasks.details: Create a `@ControllerAdvice` class to handle common exceptions. Implement specific handlers (`@ExceptionHandler`) for `ResourceNotFoundException`, validation exceptions (`MethodArgumentNotValidException`), and a general handler for any other server errors. Responses should be a standardized JSON object with fields like `timestamp`, `status`, `error`, and `message`.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually trigger different error conditions in integration tests. For example, request an entity that doesn't exist and verify the 404 response format. Send a POST request with missing required fields and verify the 400 response format.

tasks.title: Configure and Refine OpenAPI (Swagger) Documentation
tasks.description: Set up and annotate the controllers to generate clear and interactive API documentation using SpringDoc/Swagger.
tasks.details: The `springdoc-openapi-ui` dependency is already present. Add `@Operation`, `@ApiResponse`, and `@Parameter` annotations to all methods in `NewsArticleController` to describe what each endpoint does, its parameters, and possible responses. Configure global API info like title and version. Verify the documentation is accessible and accurate at `/swagger-ui.html`.
tasks.testStrategy: Start the application and navigate to the Swagger UI URL. Review the generated documentation for each endpoint. Check for clarity, completeness, and correctness of descriptions, parameters, and example schemas.

tasks.title: Implement Unit and Integration Tests
tasks.description: Write a comprehensive suite of unit and integration tests for the service and controller layers to ensure functionality and robustness.
tasks.details: For the service layer (`NewsArticleService`), write unit tests using Mockito to mock the repository and verify the business logic. For the controller layer (`NewsArticleController`), write integration tests using `@SpringBootTest` and `MockMvc` to test the full HTTP request-response cycle for all CRUD endpoints, including pagination and error handling.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the full test suite using Maven (`mvn test`). Ensure all tests pass and achieve a reasonable code coverage percentage. The tests themselves are the validation for this task.

subtasks.title: Design and Implement User Authentication Database Schema
subtasks.description: Create the necessary database tables to store user information, including credentials, profiles, and session tokens.
subtasks.details: Create a `users` table with columns like `id`, `email` (unique), `password_hash`, `created_at`. Create a `sessions` table for managing user login sessions with `id`, `user_id` (foreign key), `token`, and `expires_at`. Use a database migration tool to apply the schema.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a unit test to verify the migration runs successfully and creates the tables with the correct columns, constraints, and relationships. Manually inspect the database schema after running the migration.

subtasks.title: Develop User Registration API Endpoint
subtasks.description: Create a public API endpoint (e.g., `POST /api/auth/register`) that allows new users to create an account.
subtasks.details: The endpoint should accept `email` and `password`. It must validate the input (e.g., password strength, valid email format). Hash the password using a strong algorithm like bcrypt before storing it in the `users` table. Return a success message or an appropriate error (e.g., 409 Conflict for existing email).
subtasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests to cover successful registration, registration with a duplicate email, and registration with invalid input data (e.g., weak password, invalid email format). Verify the password stored in the database is correctly hashed.

subtasks.title: Develop User Login API Endpoint
subtasks.description: Create a public API endpoint (e.g., `POST /api/auth/login`) for users to authenticate and receive a session token.
subtasks.details: The endpoint should accept `email` and `password`. It will find the user by email, retrieve the stored password hash, and compare it with the provided password. If valid, generate a secure session token (e.g., JWT), store it in the `sessions` table, and return it to the client.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests for successful login with correct credentials, failed login with an incorrect password, and failed login for a non-existent user. Verify that a valid token is returned on success and a session record is created in the database.

subtasks.title: Implement Authentication Middleware for Protected Routes
subtasks.description: Create a middleware that intercepts requests to protected API endpoints, validates the session token, and attaches the authenticated user's information to the request object.
subtasks.details: The middleware should extract the session token from the `Authorization` header. It will then look up the token in the `sessions` table, check if it's valid and not expired, and retrieve the associated user. If valid, pass the request to the next handler. If invalid, return a 401 Unauthorized error.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create a dummy protected endpoint. Write integration tests to verify that requests with a valid token are allowed, while requests with an invalid, expired, or missing token are rejected with a 401 status code.

subtasks.title: Develop User Logout API Endpoint
subtasks.description: Create a protected API endpoint (e.g., `POST /api/auth/logout`) that invalidates the user's current session token.
subtasks.details: This endpoint must be protected by the authentication middleware. It should identify the session token used for authentication and delete the corresponding record from the `sessions` table in the database, effectively invalidating the session.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write an integration test that first logs a user in to get a token, then calls the logout endpoint with that token. Verify a success status is returned. Attempt to use the same token again on a protected route and verify that it is now rejected with a 401 Unauthorized error.

tasks.title: Initialize Project with Spring Boot
tasks.description: Generate and configure the initial Spring Boot project, including core dependencies, package structure, environment profiles, and foundational DTOs.
tasks.details:
1. **Project Generation**: Use Spring Initializr (start.spring.io) to generate a new Maven project with Java and the latest stable Spring Boot version. Include the following dependencies: Spring Web, Spring Data JPA, MySQL Driver, Lombok, Validation, Spring Boot DevTools, SpringDoc OpenAPI UI, and Spring Boot Actuator.
2. **Project Structure**: Organize the codebase using a package-by-feature approach. For the 'news' feature, create a primary package `com.example.newsapi`, which will contain sub-packages for `controller`, `service`, `repository`, `entity`, and `dto`.
3. **Configuration**: Create an `application.yml` file in `src/main/resources`. Configure a `dev` profile to use an H2 in-memory database for local development (`spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb`, `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update`). Configure a `prod` profile with placeholders for MySQL connection details (`spring.datasource.url=${DB_URL}`, `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`). Set `dev` as the default active profile.
4. **DTO Definition**: Create initial Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) to decouple the API layer from the persistence layer. Define a `NewsArticleRequest` DTO with fields for creating/updating an article, annotated with Jakarta Validation constraints (e.g., `@NotBlank`). Define a `NewsArticleResponse` DTO to specify the data returned by the API, avoiding direct exposure of the JPA entity.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Run `mvn clean install` to confirm the project compiles and all dependencies are resolved without errors.
2. Start the application using `mvn spring-boot:run`. Verify that the application starts successfully on the embedded server.
3. Access the Spring Boot Actuator health endpoint at `http://localhost:8080/actuator/health` and confirm the status is `UP`.
4. Access the SpringDoc OpenAPI UI at `http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html` to ensure it loads correctly.
5. Review the project's directory structure to ensure it follows the specified package-by-feature organization.
6. Inspect the `application.yml` file to verify that both `dev` and `prod` profiles are correctly defined and that `dev` is the default.
